thread:
zoe: hi all, day 2 here. followed the runtime build-from-source guide and the docker image builds fine, but when I run the containerized smoke test it errors out immediately with:

```
/usr/bin/python3: error while loading shared libraries: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

I checked the host and it has drivers, but the container seems blind to them. any dev box setup steps I missed? who should I tag for infra?

alex_dev: welcome! :tada: quick checklist: 
- does the host show GPUs with nvidia-smi?
- are you running the container with --gpus or the nvidia runtime?
- is nvidia-container-toolkit installed on the host?

If host nvidia-smi works but the container still lacks libcuda, it's usually the toolkit/daemon config.

ben_runtime: adding runtime tips: we often see this when people build artifacts on the host and then run them in a minimal image without the driver libs exposed. try running a known cuda image to isolate: 
```
docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.8-base nvidia-smi
```
If that shows the GPUs, then your image needs to mount driver libs or use the same base that expects host driver mounting.

maria_infra: infra policy: ubuntu 22.04 dev boxes should have nvidia-driver-515 or newer and nvidia-container-toolkit configured. confirm /etc/docker/daemon.json includes the nvidia runtime entry and restart docker after toolkit installs. also check /etc/nvidia-container-runtime/host-files-for-container.d exists and contains the json entries.

zoe: host nvidia-smi OK, shows driver 525. tried the cuda image and inside it nvidia-smi still fails with libcuda not found. i did run docker with --gpus.

alex_dev: then it sounds like the host toolkit files are missing or the cli cannot produce the mount list. run on host: nvidia-container-cli --load-kmods -k and see if it exits cleanly. also dpkg -l | grep nvidia-container to verify installation.

zoe: ran nvidia-container-cli and it choked with a missing json under /etc/nvidia-container-runtime/host-files-for-container.d, looks like a half-installed toolkit from some earlier attempt. reinstalling nvidia-container-toolkit fixed it. after reinstall, docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.8-base nvidia-smi shows GPUs and our runtime tests pass.

ben_runtime: awesome. for the onboarding doc, maybe add a short dev checklist: host nvidia-smi, toolkit installed, docker daemon runtime config, test with nvidia/cuda image, then run your runtime image with --gpus. small PR will save future new hires time.

ci-bot: ci/infra: related infra tickets exist, if this box came from terraform open ticket and assign to @maria_infra so we can fix the provisioning script.

zoe: will open a ticket and submit a tiny README PR summarizing the steps that saved me. thanks everyone :heart:
